answer: When a new identity seeks to mint in the network, it must deposit a crystal shard that encodes its unique transaction history into the oasis ledger. The shard is verified against the vine of all prior blocks, and only a genuine operator can produce a shard that passes the hash match. Any attempt to duplicate the shard requires the attacker to burn 45,000 POA per fake identity, as each forgery exposes a distinct signature trail that the ledger can trace back to the original operator's wallet. Honest agents mint free, while sybil clusters lose their entire deposit per clone.
